title: customer-questionnaire-companion
summary: Companion guide for responding to customer security questionnaires focused on RBAC v2, audit log schema, SIEM export, and evidence automation. Provides short answers, mapping to product features, and example audit event fields clients commonly ask for.
audience: Customer-facing security, Solutions Engineering, Sales Engineering, Compliance reviewers
body:
Purpose:
This note is intended to speed up and standardize responses to customer security questionnaires (Vendors, RFI, RFQ, security questionnaires) where customers ask about RBAC, auditing, and logs. It contains: canned answers, feature mappings, an example audit log schema, SIEM export options, and pointers to evidence automation artifacts.

How to use: copy the ‘Suggested customer answer’ blocks into your questionnaire response and paste the ‘Supporting detail’ into an appendix when asked for more context. If a customer requires a different export format or additional fields, open SEC-1234 and tag solutions-eng for a custom delivery.

1) RBAC (Role-Based Access Control) — Suggested answers and notes
Suggested customer answer (short):
Yes. Redwood supports RBAC v2 with scoped roles, SAML/SCIM provisioning, and custom role templates. Admins can configure role assignments via the Console or API; permissions are enforced in the control plane and at the serving runtime.
Supporting detail (copy into appendix):
- Roles shipped out-of-the-box: owner, admin, engineer, read-only, billing, support.
- Custom roles: templates with resource scoping (by org, project, model, or deployment).
- Provisioning: SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM for automated provisioning/deprovisioning.
- Enforcement: Token-level checks at the API gateway and service layer; principle of least privilege encouraged via scoped roles.
- Auditing: role assignment changes emit audit events (see Audit Log Schema).
Notes / Caveats:
- We do not currently support attribute-based access control (ABAC) policies in the Console; ABAC requests are tracked under SEC-2107.
- For private/on-prem installs we offer an optional integration layer to map external group attributes to Redwood roles during provisioning.

2) Audit log schema — Example event and guidance
Suggested customer answer (short):
Redwood emits structured audit logs for control-plane actions, authentication events, and serving-related administration. Logs are JSON-lines and include timestamps, actor identity, action, resource, outcome, and request identifiers suitable for ingestion in SIEMs.
Supporting detail (example schema fields):
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- event_type (string) e.g., "role.assignment.create", "login", "api.request", "deploy.model"
- event_id (uuid)
- actor_id (string) internal id
- actor_email (string) optional
- actor_ip (string) optional
- actor_user_agent (string) optional
- target_resource_type (string) e.g., "deployment", "model", "project", "user"
- target_resource_id (string)
- target_resource_name (string) when available
- action (string) e.g., "grant", "revoke", "create", "delete", "update"
- outcome (string) e.g., "success", "failure", "partial"
- request_id (string) correlates front-end and runtime traces
- trace_id (string) propagated to runtime for per-request correlation
- duration_ms (integer) optional
- request_payload_summary (string)  truncated/hashed when sensitive
- response_status_code (integer) optional
- error_code (string) optional
- note (string) freeform
Schema notes:
- Logs avoid storing plaintext secrets or large blobs; request_payload_summary is designed to be safe for customer ingestion (truncate/hash PII).
- We can include additional fields on request by request (contact solutions-eng).

3) SIEM export options and guidance
Suggested customer answer (short):
We support push-based log export via HTTPS (JSONL), native ingestion to cloud SIEMs via integrations (S3->SIEM connector), and syslog/CEF output through our log-forwarder appliance for Dedicated/Private customers. Exports can be configured to include control-plane audit logs, auth events, and selected runtime operational logs.
Supporting detail and options:
- Hosted customers: S3-compatible delivery (gzipped JSONL) + lifecycle controls. Typical delivery cadence: 1–5 min rollups.
- Dedicated/private: option for a log-forwarder that supports RFC5424/syslog, CEF, and Elastic ECS mappings.
- Event volume planning: estimate 10–200 events per active user per day (highly dependent on automation and API volume). Provide sample usage and we’ll help size exports.
- Security: TLS for transport, signed manifests, IAM role / presigned URLs for S3 storage.
- Mapping recommendations: provide ECS/CEF mapping templates we maintain in GitHub (linked in artifacts).

4) Evidence automation + delivery (how to attach artifacts to questionnaire)
Suggested customer answer (short):
We provide an evidence bundle process where artifacts are packaged, time-stamped, and delivered via a secure link or uploaded to customer provided S3. Many standard artifacts are available automatically (audit extracts, RBAC config snapshots, compliance check runbooks).
Supporting detail:
- Evidence bundle types: configuration snapshot, audit-log extract (timebox), role mappings, vulnerability scan report, and policy attestations.
- Artifact signing: bundles include a digest and signed manifest; for Dedicated/Private we can apply customer-managed KMS signing on request.
- Automation: SEC-evidence-bot (internal) can produce pre-formatted evidence for typical SOC2 and ISO questions; see SEC-1234 for the runbook.
- Turnaround: automated bundles for routine requests typically < 24h; custom extractions take longer.

5) Common customer questionnaire excerpts + canned responses (copy/paste friendly)
Q: Do you support SAML-based SSO and SCIM provisioning?
A: Yes. SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM for lifecycle provisioning are both supported for our Console and API access.

Q: Can you provide an extract of admin activity for the last 90 days?
A: Yes. We can provide a timeboxed audit log extract containing admin events (role change, user invite/revoke, org-level config changes). Please raise a request via the security portal or Solutions Eng ticket (SEC-1234).

Q: How do you prevent sensitive data from appearing in logs?
A: Redwood strips or truncates PII and secrets in audit logs by default. Request payloads are summarized and hashed where necessary; for high-sensitivity workloads we offer additional redaction and on-premise log filters.

6) Appendix: Example trust-center blurb for public-facing pages
Redwood Inference implements fine-grained RBAC v2 with SAML/SCIM provisioning, comprehensive audit logging, and multiple export mechanisms to integrate with customer SIEMs. Audit events are structured JSON, signed, and delivered via configurable export channels (S3, HTTPS, syslog) with encryption at-rest and in-transit. Evidence bundles for common compliance frameworks are available on request and can be automated for recurring attestations.

FAQ / open questions (internal):
- Customer asked for session-level trace IDs connecting front-end token creation to runtime token usage — need to confirm whether trace propagation across all internal hops is enabled for hosted customers (SEC-2201).
- ABAC ask: prioritize tracking ABAC feature requests under SEC-2107 and decide Q2/2026 roadmap slot.

faq:
Q: Can customers get realtime streaming of audit events?
A: For Dedicated/Private deployments we can stream events to customer endpoints (syslog/HTTPS). For hosted tenants we provide near real-time delivery via S3/HTTPS with 1–5 minute typical latency.

Q: Do logs contain request/response bodies?
A: No. We avoid storing full request/response bodies in audit logs. We provide summarized payload fields and hashes for correlation. Full request data is retained in internal operational traces with restricted access and can be exported under a formal data request.
